raw_description_in_csv: Pending activity (blank desc in parsed row)
classification_rationale: Represents a T+1 settlement debit for an equity purchase. Fidelity exports the purchased shares at market value but does not reduce SPAXX on execution day. The pending debit is the exact purchase cost. Observed in every settlement window in SIH history. Magnitude always matches a recently executed equity purchase in the same portfolio. The debit is guaranteed to reduce SPAXX within 1-2 business days. Zero-MV variant ($0.00) observed in audit_test.csv — safe to ignore (no cash impact).

Fidelity may export cash transfers-in-transit as negative pending rows. These represent cash movement between accounts, not equity settlement. Impact on deployable cash depends on direction and account structure. Without observed examples, conservative classification applies.

Pending dividends would be positive (inbound cash), not negative. A negative dividend row would be highly unusual and likely represents a tax withholding or dividend reversal. Until observed and analyzed, do not offset cash for this type.

Fidelity journal entries may appear as accounting adjustments. These could represent account rebalancing, cost basis adjustments, or fee accruals. Impact on cash varies. Without observed examples, treat as warning-only.

Zero-MV ACCOUNTING_ADJUSTMENT rows represent already-settled or stale pending rows from prior exports. The pending debit was either cancelled or settled. Subtracting $0.00 has no cash impact but including these rows in the offset computation is safe (no effect).
